newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to sack Basque officials in ETA case - paper.
newsitem.headline: Spain to sack Basque officials in ETA case - paper.

text.p: The Spanish government will dismiss two senior Basque officials for mishandling the case of an ETA guerrilla arrested last week and hospitalised two days later in serious condition, a newspaper reported on Monday.

The Spanish daily El Mundo said the Interior Ministry will recommend sacking Guipuzcoa province Civil Governor Emilio Monge and San Sebastian police chief Angel Goya for failing to inform the government that Fernando Elejalde was badly wounded upon his arrest and for neglecting to take him to a hospital sooner.
Interior Ministry officials were not immediately available for comment.

The Interior Ministry investigated whether Elejalde had been tortured during interrogation but said late on Sunday he was wounded in a gunbattle with police as he fled the scene of the killing of a prison psychologist in San Sebastian.

Elejalde was hospitalised on Thursday, two days after his arrest, with four crushed vertebrae, a ruptured kidney, a perforated eardrum and bruises. His defence lawyer said he was beaten while in police custody.

The Interior Ministry also said late on Sunday that during questioning in hospital by a Supreme Court judge at the weekend, Elejalde had admitted killing two men -- the prison psychologist Javier Garcia Elosegui and a San Sebastian bicycle vendor.
